main_text.l: quæ ex cuiusq; rei & verbi af-
Quid est Rei & verbi affectio? Est ratio,
quam quæque res & dictio habet ad alteram.
Vt Homo est species animalis: Membrum est
pars corporis. Græci λόγον appellant. Itaque
Sed vitandæ ambiguitatis caussa nomen Affe-
ctionis delegimus: quo eodé Cicero & in To-
picis & in Partitionibus hac eadem in re est
usus. Rationis autem verbum à Mathematicis
sumptum est, qui λόγον definiunt duarum eius-

page.notes: The large woodcut initial at the start of the chapter is a decorative Q-shaped letter; the first word is read as QVID. The "Q" of the woodcut is inferred and marked here, not certain. Printed "Affe-" and "af-" hyphens are kept as printed. The Greek λόγον is copied as printed. Spelling is modernised only for u/v and i/j and long s; æ, ò, Latinè and Habitū are kept as printed.
